item.title: Update
item.content:encoded:
I was reminded that I needed to update this article, and so I have.

Major changes:

  • Explained the name "Summer's Exile" (formerly only explained in what amounted to an Easter egg). Explained what "Summer" might mean.
  • Made the mythological reference to Sisyphus more explicit (the implication wasn't really coming across to readers).
  • Added more possibilities with the Foundation which weren't really implied even though they were supposed to be.
  • A few more elements made more explicit.
  • Made a bunch of minor edits for clarity & readability. Notably, I changed the biggest Jailor jab to a footnote since people found it distracting.

I haven't messed with the pronouns. I still might change to 'she' if people think that reads better, given that the Exile is not human.

item.content:encoded:
SCP-001?
What? One can speculate, right?

SCP-001.
Description: The Foundation is a memetic phenomenon that has persisted across the ages as a way to protect humanity from knowledge of the anomalous and knowledge that is anomalous in itself (quite often an overlapping concept). While the origin of this phenomenon has not been clearly determined, as is usual with memes of its magnitude, SCP-001 has been deemed not only primordial, but directly responsible for the existence of the Foundation itself. (…)

The Jailor's Dream.
Conspectus: The End of Dreams, also referred to in this day and age as "the Foundation", "the Jailor's Dream" or "the Not-Mind" is a conscious thought that can take root in all but most powerful of minds and, theoretically, wishes to prevent the Children of Dust from ever taking hold over knowledge of the Ways, the Library and the anomalous as a whole. The first cause of the End of Dreams remains removed and unattainable for the Serpent's Hand, and the archivists will not reveal any information on neither its origin nor its actual entity…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Two things to address:

Singular 'they' is the acceptable gender-neutral pronoun in English; it only fell out of favor in recent years due to attempts to make English conform to Latin rules and a backlash against feminist thought a few decades ago (but mainly, the Latin rules thing; see also split infinitives).

It's come back into favor rather recently, partly due to the rise of more people coming out of the closet as genderqueer and embracing those pronouns for themselves.

It's awkward in the sense that people aren't used to it, but it does stop being awkward when you're used to it (in most cases).

However, as for the article's concern—

Within the article itself, it's meant to imply that the Hand see "Summer's Exile" as a person who would properly be referred to this way, albeit a person who is a predator. (As opposed to 017, who they see as a straight-up scary monster, an Other Thing, and they're frightened of even TRYING to guess its gender, partly because of the taboo.)

However, I don't know that the rest of the article gets that across successfully; while I'm very happy with the present form of the article, I will be tweaking that post-contest.

If it's easier, I may end up changing the pronouns to "she/her" and save the singular "they" for an article that's about … well, an actually humanoid person who is actually genderqueer, so it's only as confusing as it has to be.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That just seems like a poorly-done jab at the Foundation.

Well, that's because that's exactly what it is.

The Hand isn't a monolith, and each Hand article has multiple contributors. That's just the POV of one of the more radical Hand members — who, I agree, is being pretty unfair. The writer of the hub intro piece would also agree that's unfair, too, even (probably taking the POV that the Foundation cares about scientific inquiry, but are hampering themselves out of sheer fear — a POV that's more fairly reflected in established material). But… the more unfair POV still exists. Hell, more extreme perspectives exist.

Post-contest I'll add a footnote disagreeing with it, and/or change that into a footnote or alter it in some other way. Because why not, eh? If you come away thinking that's meant to represent the Hand's POV overall, others may, too.
